newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up backed by locals.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up backed by locals.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Monday supported by domestic buyers, but analysts said it was doubtful the index could maintain its current momentum in the absence of foreign players.
The all share index closed 4.42 points up at 617.52. Price gainers led decliners 48 to seven. Dipped Products rose one rupee to 83 and Sampath Bank 1.50 to 49.50.
"What began as a push by retail investors now also includes local institutional investors," said Namal Kamalgoda, fund manager at CTC Eagle Fund Management.
Local investor sentiment has improved on the back of good corporate growth expected in 1997, he said. But the low level of foreign investment was worrying, Kamalgoda said.
Turnover was 28.6 million on 1.1 million shares. Foreign buying was 5.2 million, while selling was 4.4 million.
It was, however, encouraging to note that local investors have regained confidence in the market, said Rohan Fernando, a trader at brokerage CT Smith.
Domestic confidence was at a low ebb in 1995 and 1996, due to an escalation of the northeast conflict, a crippling drought and power cuts. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
